synopsis: ISO 13849 is presented as a generic machinery control-system safety standard, while ISO 19014 is the appropriate sector framework for earth-moving machines; the safety-case skeleton uses ISO 13849 or IEC 62061 where ISO 19014 does not reach [f15007, f15168, f15272]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, preparing that skeleton by mid-2027 is considered realistic; the intervention path needs a performance-level or integrity assignment and fault testing, although the relevant editions were not verified [f829, f7455]. The glossary describes risk-based Performance Level selection, common-cause-failure defenses, and four diagnostic-coverage bands: below 60%, 60–90%, 90–99%, and at least 99%; it also cautions that ISO 13849 does not itself assign the required level for the collision function [f11972, f12115, f12126, f15264]. For most markets, the booklet identifies the manufacturer's internal safety board working under ISO 19014 and ISO 13849, together with customers, as accepting the evidence [f1613, f12288]. These recommendations remain qualified: ISO 13849 was not reviewed in full text, simulation-evidence acceptance and tool-qualification rules were not verified, and the automatic-brake safety-function claim relies on draft evidence [f8942, f11198, f6580].
